decision_conditions: The proposed development, by virtue of the number of potential occupants and proposed use, would represent an over-intensification of the unit which would be harmful to the amenities of the neighbouring properties and at odds with the established character of the surrounding locality. The proposal would have an unacceptable and undue impact on existing residential amenity in terms of noise and disturbance, over and above what would be expected for a single family dwelling. As such, the proposal would therefore be contrary to Policy EM8 of the Hillingdon Local Plan - Part 1: Strategic Policies (2012), Policies DMH 5 and DMHB 11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 - Development Management Policies (2020), Policy D14 of the London Plan (2021), and Policy P3 2b of the NPPF (2026).

In the absence of any quantifiable details or evidence with regard to the level of present on-street parking demand within the locality and whether any spare capacity exists which could satisfactorily accommodate the potential parking displacement generated by the proposed level of occupancy, it is considered that the 'car free' proposal has the potential to lead to undue on-street parking displacement to the detriment of parking capacity and safety on the local public highway. As such, the proposal would be contrary to Policies DMH 5, DMT 1, DMT 2 and DMT 6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020) and Policy T4 of the London Plan (2021).

The proposed development, by virtue of its layout, internal design, number of potential occupants, and lack of private external amenity space, would present a living environment which would be neither comfortable or practical, nor fit for the intended purpose. Additionally, all proposed bedrooms would fail to meet the required minimum space standards, and in two cases the minimum width requirements, whilst the proposal would also fail to provide adequate communal space and facilities for the occupiers. Considered altogether, the proposed development would provide a significantly sub-standard and unsatisfactory level of internal and external living accommodation for the occupiers. As such, the proposal would conflict with Policies DMH 5, DMHB 16 and DMHB 18 of the Local Plan, and Policies D3 and D6 of the London Plan (2021).

The proposed development, in the absence of any submitted details, fails to effectively demonstrate that sufficient and suitable provision for well-designed storage refuse space could be provided on-site, as well as suitable provision for secure and accessible cycle parking for the occupiers.  As such, in the absence of such provisions, the proposal would be contrary to Policies DMH 5, DMHB 11 and DMT 5 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part Two - Development Management Policies (2020) and Policies D6, SI 7 and T5 of the London Plan (2021).
description: Conversion of existing residential dwelling (Class C3) into a 6-bedroom HMO (Class C4) (Retrospective).
